 1.
The petitioner is an accused in connection with Muribahal P.S. Case No.313 of 2023 corresponding to Special G.R. Case No.103 of 2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 313/417/376(2)(n)
of the IPC read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act pending in the Court of the learned Special Judge (POCSO), Balangir.
The petitioner had approached the learned Additional District Judge-cum-Special Judge under POCSO Act, Balangir in Special G.R. No.103 of 2023 praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 27.02.2024 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
3.

The prosecution case as per the F.I.R. is that, on 23.11.2023, the complainant reported at Muribahal P.S. alleging that, in the year 2017, the present petitioner had proposed the victim and by giving her assurance of marriage, had kept physical relationship with her since then.
The victim became pregnant.
The present petitioner forcefully gave her medicine and aborted her pregnancy.
Thereafter, the petitioner denied to marry the victim.

Hence, the F.I.R.

sentences.text: During the investigation, the statement of the victim, who was 19 years old, was recorded under Section 164 of the Cr. P.C.
She, in her statement, has stated that, in the year 2017, when she was 17 years old, she had relationship with the present petitioner.
The petitioner, on the assurance of marriage, had committed sexual assault to her.
Subsequently, he had wriggled out of his promise to marry her.

5. From the evidence collected by the prosecution, which form part of the charge sheet, the nature of accusation and the age of both the victim (19 years) and the accused (25 years), it can be inferred that this is neither a case of perpetration of sexual exploitation or abuse nor emotional obtrude caused to the vulnerable minor girl, rather it's love affair, which appears to have gone sour.
Therefore, the accused is entitled to bail.
6. The F.I.R. was registered on 23.11.2023.
The petitioner has been in custody since 24.11.2023.

7. Regard being had to the nature of the accusation and the period of custody of the petitioner i.e.
since 24.11.2023, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

In the event the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
9. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge Subhasis Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack.
